import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders INVITATION_FORMAT = """

{event_title}

{event_description}

Date: {event_date}

{additional_notes}
""" def create_event_invitation(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a secure HTML representation of an event invitation. Parameters ---------- title : str The title or name of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event (may include multiple paragraphs and formatting). date : str The scheduled date of the event. notes : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the event organizer. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML string suitable for safe rendering in a web page. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is missing or empty. """ # Basic validation if not all(isinstance(arg, str) and arg.strip() for arg in (title, description, date)): raise ValueError("Title, description, and date must be non-empty strings.") # Escape all user-supplied content to prevent XSS safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(description, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") safe_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) safe_notes = html.escape(notes or "", quote=False).replace("\n", "
") # Render the template invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes ) return invitation_html.strip()
